title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Custom Fabric Swatch Materials
description: CLO technical experts will guide you step-by-step in learning custom zipper pull material creation techniques, making your designs more diverse!
transcript:
How to Make a Zip-Up Puller  
Now open CLO.  
Today I will explain how to make a zip-up puller.  
In the previous tutorial video,  
we showed how to make a zip-up puller  
and then attach it as an accessory to the clothes.  
However, you couldn’t really pull the zip-up puller.  
In our new version,  
we can easily define the zip-up puller as a zip-up puller,  
which achieves a more realistic pull effect.  
Now let’s make a zip-up puller like this.  
There is a reference picture of a zip-up puller in your material.  
This is the zip-up puller we are going to make today.  

First, let’s make a zip-up puller.  
Find the zip-up tool in the 2D window.  
Use the default size of 500mm x 500mm.  
Click OK.  
Then we will add the reference picture of the zip-up puller as a sticker.  
Click OK.  
This is the zip-up puller we are going to make today.  

Next,  
we will adjust the transparency of the sticker a little bit  
to make it easier for us to draw the outline and the inner lines.  
Then we need to use the inner line tool  
to draw its outline.  
You can see in our reference picture of this zip-up puller  
that the puller and its main body  
have different thicknesses.  
So,  
we need to make the zip-up puller thinner,  
and the main body a little bit thicker.  
Thus, we need to create two panels  
and set the thickness of the zip-up puller accordingly.  

We are now using the multi-sided line tool.  
First, draw the outline of this zip-up puller.  
Make it smooth.  
Focus on the pace using this palette tool.  
Press CTRL  
to design the curve of the zip-up puller.  
Choose Line.  
Here, we use the geometry of this zip-up puller.  

Next, let’s draw the curve inside.  
We can adjust the position of the curve points  
with the help of a ruler.  
Slightly adjust the curve of the curve points.  
Because the size of the curve is relatively small,  
there may be some uneven edges.  
We need to make some minor adjustments to it.  

If we want to move the straight line point,  
just press D on the keyboard,  
drag the straight line point,  
and press D on the keyboard again.  

After the adjustment is almost done,  
we can directly select its outline.  
Just cut it off directly with the right button.  
Because the particle diameter of the current one is 20,  
the pattern drawn now  
is a triangular grid.  
Adjust the pattern example to 1.  

Then let’s go to the main body of the drawing.  
Use the internal multidirectional line tool  
to draw the main body of the drawing.  
Press the Shift key to make it a trajectory.  
Let’s make this line smoother.  
Then we can adjust the curve of the curve points.  
Let’s make a closed pattern.  
Then we can adjust the inner outline.  
This inner line can be deleted.  
Then right-click and select Cut.  
We don’t need this big board;  
it can be deleted.  

Next, we will turn the outline line inside it into a hole,  
including the pull ring, which also needs to be converted into a hole.  
Then we can delete all its stickers.  
Use the adjustment sticker tool  
to delete the stickers on these boards.  

Finally, we can adjust the curve.  
We can see that the main body of the puller is different from the back of the puller,  
so we choose the main body of the puller,  
increase its rendering thickness to 4,  
and adjust its curve.  
Its pull ring is the same;  
we can increase its rendering thickness by 1 mm,  
and adjust the curve to 25%.  

Then we can delete all its stickers.  
Select all the elements,  
and then we can move the puller.  
We can choose the size of the puller.  
We can change the size of the puller  
and see the result of the puller.  

Next, I will teach you how to make this kind of logo with a three-dimensional metal engraving effect.  
We need to use a sticker to create this effect.  
Before making it, we need to prepare an image of this effect.  
There is also an image of the texture of the sticker.  
The most important thing is this line drawing.  
This is the key to making our logo present the three-dimensional metal engraving effect.  

We find the sticker option in the object window.  
Then we drag the texture of the sticker in.  
Then drag the texture in again.  
Add this sticker to our template.  
This sticker is relatively large,  
so we need to adjust its angle.  
Adjust it to 90 degrees.  
Then we need to adjust its size.  
When adjusting the size, right-click to enter its size.  
I entered 4.5 mm.  
Click OK.  

Now our sticker is added,  
but actually, we don’t need this texture.  
We only need the effect of its line drawing.  
Then how should we proceed?  
Select this sticker in the object window.  
Adjust its shadow intensity to 50.  
Remember to fill the color.  
Then adjust the shadow brightness to 50.  
Adjust the shadow intensity to -50.  
Adjust the shadow brightness to 50.  

Now we keep the auto effect of the line drawing.  
The texture is processed to the brightest and whitest effect.  
Then we can enhance the strength of the line drawing  
and modify the texture of the sticker to metal.  
Finally, we get the metal effect  
and the effect of the logo with the auto effect.  

Now we have finished making the puller with the template.  
Next, we need to export OBJ.  
Before exporting OBJ, we need to pre-select.  
Pre-select all the templates.  
Then right-click in the 3D window.  
Choose Move to Ground Center.  
Then we need to use the positioning tool.  
Drag it to the bottom of the ground.  
We need to let the ground line pass through the middle of the puller.  
This step is very important.  
This step determines that we will define the template as a puller.  
The puller is positioned at the puller head.  
We need to place all the pullers in this position,  
with the hole passing through the ground line.  

Then select File.  
Select Export.  
Select OBJ.  
Name it puller1.  
Then click Save.  

What we need to pay attention to is:  
we need to select all the templates,  
and select all the stickers and accessories.  
Select More Targets.  
Select Latter.  
Select Internal Shape.  
Save with Document.  
Click Confirm.  

Open the project file that needs to replace the puller.  
Let’s open the file that we just saved.  
Find the compressed file.  
Unzip the compressed file.  
We can see here,  
there is an OBJ file.  

Then we go back to CLO.  
In the top menu bar,  
find Material.  
Then find Puller.  
There is a self-defined OBJ option at the bottom of the puller.  
Type select Puller.  
The name can be self-defined.  
Click the button behind the OBJ file.  
Click the button.  
Select the OBJ file that has just been unzipped.  
Select Open.  
This file is added in,  
and you can check it in the preview.  
Click Confirm.  
There will be a pop-up window.  
Click Confirm.  

Now let’s click this puller.  
In the puller here,  
you can see the puller preset we just created.  
You will see that this puller is relatively large.  
So when we first input it,  
you need to adjust its size.  

I’m going to input it again now.  
Select Material.  
Puller Self-Defined OBJ.  
In the proportion here,  
we should choose a smaller proportion.  
Select this OBJ file.  
We can adjust the proportion to 40%.  
Then click Confirm.  

Again, create this puller preset.  
Select the second one.  
Now it is a suitable size.  
We can adjust its slanting angle,  
then modify its material type.  

Now this self-defined puller is made,  
and it retains the effect of the three-dimensional logo.  

The above is the self-defined puller tutorial.  
At the bottom is the self-defined puller.  
We can adjust the length.  
At the bottom is the self-defined puller.  
Then we can adjust the length,  
and then we can adjust the width.  
For this, we can change the width,  
so we can adjust the length.

chunks.content: ## Creating a Zip-Up Puller in CLO This section explains how to create a realistic zip-up puller accessory in CLO using reference images, drawing tools, and layering techniques. It covers the use of inner lines, thickness adjustments, and panel creation to differentiate parts of the puller for a more authentic effect. 1. **Starting the Zip-Up Puller Project** - Open CLO and select the zip-up tool in the 2D window. - Use the default size of 500mm x 500mm and confirm. - Add a reference picture of the zip-up puller as a sticker and adjust its transparency for easier tracing. 2. **Drawing the Zip-Up Puller Outline** - Use the inner line tool to draw the outer shape of the puller. - The puller consists of two parts with different thicknesses: the thinner puller itself and a thicker main body. - Create two panels to represent these parts accordingly. - Use the multi-sided line tool to draw smooth curves; hold CTRL to adjust curves precisely. - Use a ruler to adjust curve points and minimize uneven edges. 3. **Editing Line Points and Patterns** - To move straight line points, press D, drag the point, and press D again to lock. - Cut off the outline by right-clicking. - Adjust the particle diameter of the pattern to 1 (from the default triangular grid of 20) for better detail. 4. **Main Body Drawing and Hole Creation** - Use the internal multidirectional line tool with Shift pressed to create smooth, closed trajectories for the puller's main body. - Delete unnecessary inner lines by right-clicking and selecting Cut. - Convert the outline lines and pull ring elements into holes. - Remove all stickers using the adjustment sticker tool. 5. **Final Adjustments on Curves and Thickness** - Increase the rendering thickness of the main body to 4mm. - Adjust the pull ring’s rendering thickness by 1mm and set its curve to 25%. - Delete all remaining stickers and select all elements to move or resize the puller. - Adjust the puller size as needed and preview the results. --- ## Creating a 3D Metal Engraving Logo Effect on the Puller This section details the process of applying a three-dimensional metal engraving effect to a logo on the zip-up puller using stickers in CLO. 1. **Preparing the Sticker** - Prepare an image containing the line drawing essential for the 3D metal engraving effect. - Use the sticker option in the object window and add the texture image twice. - Add the sticker to the puller template. - Rotate the sticker 90 degrees and resize it precisely by right-clicking and entering a size of 4.5mm. 2. **Adjusting Sticker Properties for Metal Effect** - Select the sticker and adjust shadow intensity to 50. - Fill the color and adjust shadow brightness to 50. - Set shadow intensity to -50 to invert shading and maintain shadow brightness at 50. - This process creates the bright, white effect needed for the metal engraving.

chunks.content: - Add the sticker to the puller template. - Rotate the sticker 90 degrees and resize it precisely by right-clicking and entering a size of 4.5mm. 2. **Adjusting Sticker Properties for Metal Effect** - Select the sticker and adjust shadow intensity to 50. - Fill the color and adjust shadow brightness to 50. - Set shadow intensity to -50 to invert shading and maintain shadow brightness at 50. - This process creates the bright, white effect needed for the metal engraving. - Enhance line drawing strength and modify the sticker texture to a metal material to finalize the effect. --- ## Exporting and Importing the Zip-Up Puller as a Custom OBJ This section covers exporting the completed puller as an OBJ file and importing it into CLO as a self-defined puller for use in garments. 1. **Preparing the Puller for Export** - Pre-select all components of the puller template. - In the 3D window, right-click and choose "Move to Ground Center." - Use the positioning tool to align the puller so that the ground line passes through its hole; this alignment defines the puller’s pivot point. - This positioning is critical to ensure proper placement when attaching the puller later. 2. **Exporting the OBJ File** - Go to File > Export > OBJ. - Name the file (e.g., "puller1") and save. - Ensure all templates, stickers, and accessories are selected. - Select options such as "More Targets," "Latter," and "Internal Shape." - Save with the Document option and confirm. 3. **Importing the OBJ into CLO** - Open the target CLO project where the puller will be used. - Unzip the exported file to access the OBJ. - In CLO’s top menu, navigate to Material > Puller. - Use the self-defined OBJ option at the bottom of the puller selections. - Click the button to select the OBJ file and open it. - Confirm the import; a preview will appear. 4. **Adjusting Size and Material** - The imported puller may appear large initially. - Adjust the size proportion (e.g., to 40%) upon import. - Create a puller preset with the adjusted size. - Modify the slanting angle and material type as needed. - The imported puller retains the 3D metal logo engraving effect. --- ## Customizing Puller Dimensions This brief section explains how to adjust the dimensions of the self-defined puller after import. - Puller length and width can be customized. - Adjust the length and width parameters to fit the garment design requirements. - Dimension adjustments impact the visual and functional aspects of the puller on the clothing. --- This document provides a comprehensive guide to creating, texturing, exporting, importing, and customizing a zip-up puller accessory in CLO with realistic effects and precise dimension control.
